questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Honestly, it was absolute shite. The professors have too much of a say about how they want to run their individual courses, and their personal opinion of students shines through in the grading. There is no transparency (in some courses) irt. what topics/formats there will be in the exams, and the grading system consists of a ton different small grades that accumulate to the total grade, but you can still risk failing the course overall, so all the work does not necessarily pay off. Grades are also posted reaaally late, so you are never sure whether you are passing or not. Despite this, there are constant assignments etc..
Some of the professors are good, are structured and transparent in both their expectations and the teaching. Others were however very very bad, which honestly sadly has left me with a bad opinion of the host university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very intimate, small classes with max. 20 people in attendance, as small classrooms instead of lecture halls. Could actually have led to a great framework for learning well, but instead some of the professors seemed to struggle with their own ego.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

Empirical Perspective on Economic Growth: same reasons; somewhat organized, good professors, useful topics and a decent workload
